newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Menem calls for single currency in Mercosur.
newsitem.headline: Menem calls for single currency in Mercosur.

text.p: Argentina's President Carlos Menem called Monday for South America's Mercosur customs union to work towards the creation of a single currency modelled on the plans of the European union.
"We have to move seriously and quickly on the need to create, with the same Maastricht requisites, a common currency for the region," Menem told a bankers meeting in Buenos Aires.

Argentina's partners in Mercosur include Brazil, Uruguay and Paraguay. The bloc looks set to include new members in South America, and Menem added that a single currency should eventually include "the whole continent."

Menem's call followed similar recent declarations by his Economy Minister Roque Fernandez. But Brazil's Finance Minister Pedro Malan poured cold water on the idea in late April, reminding reporters that it took the European Union decades to begin work on a single currency.
"Some things in life take time. This is one of them," Malan said, "This is not a matter for tomorrow's headlines."

Members of the European Union is working to set up a single currency by 1999. But only countries which comply with tough targets for financial and economic solidity agreed in the Dutch town of Maastricht are supposed to be able to join.
Argentina's government has boasted that it meets the Maastricht criteria for low inflation, public debt and currency stability.
